channel.title: Pixelburg Post
channel.description: Fictional sample stories for offline demos and tests. Not real news: the outlet, the events and the quotes are invented; the places are real so the map can show them.

item.title: Lisbon opens a new riverside tram line
item.description: Lisbon has opened a new tram line along the Tagus river. The city says the 9 kilometre route will carry 40,000 passengers a day and cut car traffic in the old town. “This line will change how people move around the old town,” the mayor said.

item.title: Kenya switches on its largest solar farm near Nairobi
item.description: A solar farm north of Nairobi has started supplying power to the national grid. Officials say it can light around 300,000 homes and is the biggest in East Africa so far.

item.title: Iceland volcano erupts again on the Reykjanes peninsula
item.description: A fissure eruption has started again on the Reykjanes peninsula in Iceland. Scientists say lava is flowing away from nearby towns and flights are not affected.

item.title: Heavy rain floods streets in coastal towns of Kerala
item.description: Heavy monsoon rain has flooded streets in several coastal towns in Kerala, India. Local authorities have opened 120 relief camps and closed schools for two days.

item.title: Peru archaeologists uncover a 3,000-year-old temple in the Andes
item.description: Archaeologists in Peru say they have found the remains of a temple about 3,000 years old in the northern Andes. The team found painted walls and a ceremonial stairway.

item.title: Japan's bullet trains mark a record year for punctuality
item.description: Rail operators in Japan say their bullet trains ran with an average delay of under one minute last year, a record. More than 160 million passengers used the network.

item.title: Paris unveils plans to plant 170,000 trees by 2030
item.description: The city of Paris has announced plans to plant 170,000 trees by 2030 to cool the city in summer. Squares near the Seine will be the first to change.

item.title: Storm forces ferry cancellations across the Greek islands
item.description: Strong winds have forced ferry operators to cancel sailings between Athens and several Greek islands. Coast guard officials expect services to resume on Friday.

item.title: Brazil reports a sharp fall in Amazon deforestation
item.description: Brazil's space agency says deforestation in the Amazon fell by 30 percent over the past twelve months. Satellite images show the lowest level of clearing in a decade.

item.title: Wellington schools trial a four-day week
item.description: Ten schools in Wellington, New Zealand, will trial a four-day week for one term. Education officials say they want to measure the effect on attendance and wellbeing.

item.title: Canada and Mexico sign an agreement on clean water projects
item.description: Canada and Mexico have signed an agreement to fund clean water projects in rural communities. The two governments will share the cost of 50 new treatment plants.

item.title: Moderate earthquake shakes northern Chile, no damage reported
item.description: A magnitude 5.8 earthquake shook northern Chile on Tuesday morning. Emergency services say there are no reports of damage or injuries.

item.title: Cairo museum opens a new wing for ancient wooden boats
item.description: A museum in Cairo has opened a new wing to show two ancient wooden boats. Curators say the larger boat is 43 metres long and was rebuilt from 1,200 pieces.

item.title: Seoul festival lights up the Han river with 1,000 drones
item.description: A festival in Seoul lit up the sky over the Han river with a show of 1,000 drones. Organisers said about 200,000 people watched from the riverbanks.

item.title: Climate talks in Nairobi – live
item.description: Follow the latest from the climate talks in Nairobi, where ministers from 40 countries are meeting this week.
